objective: Create and configure systemd service units, including drop-in overrides, and troubleshoot them
secondaryObjectives: Troubleshoot a service that fails to start using systemctl status, journalctl and its unit file
Manage packages and repositories with apt and dnf: search, install, verify, update, remove and add a repository

sources.cite: Linux Foundation Certified System Administrator (LFCS): Domains & Competencies, Operations Deployment 25%
sources.note: Relevant text: Operations Deployment, 'Diagnose, identify, manage, and troubleshoot processes and services'. Read as the page's HTML on 2026-11-14 (page last modified 2026-10-30).

Relevant text: Restart=, 'If set to no (the default), the service will not be restarted'; 'If set to on-failure, the service will be restarted when the process exits with a non-zero exit code', and on an unclean signal; RestartSec= 'Defaults to 100ms'; 'service restart is subject to unit start rate limiting configured with StartLimitIntervalSec= and StartLimitBurst='. Read through a summarizing fetch 2026-11-14.

Relevant text: systemd.unit(5), 'Along with a unit file foo.service, a "drop-in" directory foo.service.d/ may exist. All files with the suffix ".conf" from this directory will be merged'; 'Drop-in files in /etc/ take precedence over those in /run/ which in turn take precedence over those in /usr/lib/'; /usr/lib/systemd/system holds 'System units installed by the distribution package manager'. systemctl(1), edit: 'Otherwise, a drop-in file will be created or edited' (default name override.conf) and 'After the editing is finished, configuration is reloaded, equivalent to systemctl daemon-reload'; daemon-reload 'reload all unit files'; cat may not match 'the system manager's understanding' if files changed without daemon-reload. Read through summarizing fetches 2026-11-14. That a package upgrade replaces its own file under /usr/lib is how package managers treat files that are not configuration files (dpkg(1) conffile handling, read 2026-11-14); the warning text after an unreloaded change is authored in systemd's style.

brief.situation: You look after billing1, a Fedora-family server that runs invoicer, the invoice renderer, for Harlow and Pine Supplies (fictional). It crashed at 03:10 and nothing has rendered since. Last month, after a similar crash, a colleague added Restart=on-failure to the service. Finance sends the morning invoice batch at 09:50.
handover: invoicer comes from the vendor's package; it renders PDFs dropped in /srv/invoicer/inbox and there is a /srv/invoicer/quarantine for files it cannot handle.
The colleague left a prepared drop-in at /root/override.conf ([Service] Restart=on-failure, RestartSec=5s).
howItWorks: Run commands from the command line: type one, or pick it from the suggestions or the action list. Only this lab's commands run; there is no free shell, and each command's arguments are fixed.
Each command takes operator time: run it, then let it finish, which moves the clock by the minutes it takes. The outage keeps developing on the same clock.
The map shows each host, disk or service and the links between them, with a status in words. Output appears in the terminal as it happens.
When you declare the service restored, you write the incident record and explain your reasoning.

source.note: How many operator minutes each command takes, and when the fictional outage spreads, are teaching simplifications for exam practice, not measured values. Finance sends the batch at 09:50, 30 minutes after the start.

writeup.question: For the incident record: why invoicer stayed down, why last month's fix did not hold, and why yours will.

parts.label: Cause
parts.criteria: Names the malformed PDF that crashed it, and the restart policy lost because it was edited into the vendor file under /usr/lib that Tuesday's update replaced.
parts.modelAnswer: invoicer took SIGSEGV on 0310-harlow.pdf; Restart= defaults to no, and last month's Restart=on-failure lived in /usr/lib/systemd/system/invoicer.service, which the 10 November upgrade replaced.

parts.label: Evidence
parts.criteria: Uses systemctl status, journalctl -u and systemctl cat (or show -p Restart) before changing anything.
parts.modelAnswer: status: failed, core-dump at 03:10; journal: the PDF it was rendering; systemctl cat: no Restart= and no drop-in; dnf history: upgraded Tuesday.

parts.label: Fix
parts.criteria: Quarantines only the bad file (never clears the queue), puts Restart= in a drop-in under /etc with systemctl edit or with daemon-reload, starts the service and checks the loaded value.
parts.modelAnswer: Moved the PDF to quarantine, systemctl edit invoicer with Restart=on-failure and RestartSec=5s (edit reloads the manager), started it, and systemctl show -p Restart said on-failure.

scoring.modelReasoning: Restart= defaults to no, so one crash leaves the service down. Last month's Restart= was edited into /usr/lib, which the package owns and its update replaced. Quarantine the PDF that crashed it (not the whole queue), put Restart= in a drop-in under /etc (systemctl edit reloads for you; a copied file needs daemon-reload), start it, and read the loaded value with systemctl show.
